problem.question: Martin went to a store to buy a new television set. He decided to spend no more than $1,000 and the sales clerk offered him the TV for $100 less and an additional 20% off. How much lower was the price of the television than the amount Martin decided to spend?
problem.answer:
The seller has offered him the TV for 1000 - 100 = $<<1000-100=900>>900.
The discount on the television was 900 * 20/100 = $<<900*20/100=180>>180.
The final price of the television is therefore 900 - 180 = $<<900-180=720>>720.
Martin was able to save 1000 - 720 = $<<1000-720=280>>280.
#### 280

generation.text:
The sales clerk offered Martin the TV for $100 less, so the price of the TV was $1000 - $100 = $900.
The TV had an additional 20% off, so the price of the TV was 20/100*$900 = $180 less than the price of the TV without the discount.
The final price of the TV was $900 - $180 = $720.
The price of the TV was $1000 - $720 = $280 lower than the amount Martin decided to spend.
The final answer is \boxed{280}.
